title: Kitchener Utilities clean energy transition plan endorsed
subtitle: Also: downtown event noise exemptions, a hospital foundation rally, and a regional self-employment program agreement.
overview: The Community and Infrastructure Services Committee recommended endorsing the project phases and approach for the Kitchener Utilities Clean Energy Transition {{vote:m4}}. The work is a multi-decade strategy for the city-owned natural gas utility. Phase one in 2023 is engagement, phase two in 2024 assesses options, and phase three builds an implementation plan to 2030 and beyond. Public and customer engagement is planned for September, and staff expect to report back on what they heard at the end of the year.

The committee also recommended noise exemptions for the downtown special events calendar {{vote:m1}} and for the Grand River Hospital Foundation Rally for Health at 969 King St W on May 27, with sound checks the evening before {{vote:m2}}. Staff said they would make further efforts to notify downtown residents about noisy events.

In addition, the committee recommended authorizing staff to sign funding agreements with the Region of Waterloo for the Self Employment Ontario Works program {{vote:m3}}. These are recommendations to Council, which will make the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended endorsing the project phases and approach for the Kitchener Utilities Clean Energy Transition, as outlined in report INS-2023-199 {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended granting an exemption to the Noise by-law for the downtown special events listed in Schedule A of report CSD-2023-168 {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended a noise exemption for the Grand River Hospital Foundation Rally for Health on May 27 in the Sun Life parking lot at 969 King St W, with a further exemption for sound checks on May 26 {{vote:m2}}.

The committee recommended authorizing the General Manager of Development Services to sign funding agreements with the Region of Waterloo for the Self Employment Ontario Works program, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction {{vote:m3}}.

debate: On downtown noise, one councillor asked whether the Victoria Park neighbourhood group had been consulted and whether condo residents would actually learn of events. Staff said they share event lists with condo boards and property managers and would follow up with the group. A councillor asked for a letter to every unit if complaints continue.

Another councillor cautioned against adding layers of process for events. Staff said larger events with alcohol or thousands of attendees come to Council so it can add conditions. Staff preferred leaving notification to their discretion over a formal process.

On the clean energy transition, councillors asked whether the phases move fast enough for the 2030 and 2050 emissions targets. One pointed to Quebec's heating rules and asked what the city could do to speed up provincial action. Staff said consultation runs through September, and that scalable solutions exist but take time and planning.

A councillor asked whether any increase to the emissions target would come back to Council. Staff confirmed it would. They said this project covers only the utility's line of business, and corporate target costing is separate work that will go to a Council strategic session.

Several members urged caution because the city owns a gas utility, and some stressed the risk of relying on unproven carbon capture technology. Others asked for local trades training, access to cooling for vulnerable residents, and a mayor's question on building in checkpoints, which staff said the strategy would include to adapt to changing conditions.
